texts.text: A dome, a river and fourteen places to sleep, on 118 acres above Arenal.

The Vessyl is a hotel in Arenal, Costa Rica, built around a dome made for sound. Fourteen units sit apart from one another across the property, so getting from your bed to dinner is a walk through forest rather than a hallway.

There is a river you can swim in, horses, a kitchen that changes its menu every day, and a founder who lives here. Some people come for three nights and never leave the land. Some drive up for one session in the Dome and go back to their hotel in town. Both are the right way to do this.

Fourteen units,
no two the same

Six villas, one treehouse and seven glamping tents, placed so that each one faces something different. Choose by the view, by how much privacy you want, and by how far you feel like walking to dinner. The treehouse books out first, every season.
The Dome is the reason this place exists

A dome of wood and glass at the high point of the property. Inside, sound arrives through the floor as much as through the air, so you feel the low end in your chest before you have decided what you think of it. At night it is lit, and you can see it from the far side of the valley. Sessions run most days, and you do not have to be staying here to sit in one.
You do not have to stay here to come here

Six things you can book online, with a date and a card, whether you are staying with us or at a hotel in town. A half day on the property. A sound session in the Dome. The volcano after dark. A ride along the river. An evening with whoever is playing.
You find out what is for dinner when you sit down

The kitchen cooks what came out of the garden that morning and what arrived from the valley that afternoon, so the menu is written late and it changes every night. You eat at a long table with whoever else is here. If you would rather not, tell us and we will seat you on your own, and nobody will make it strange.

Thirty-three guests, fourteen units, the Dome, the kitchen and 118 acres, with nobody else on the land. You run your programme. We run everything around it: rooms, food, sound, transport and staff. Most groups stay three to five days.

Arenal is a volcano, a lake, hot springs, waterfalls and a town called La Fortuna at the foot of all of it. Most people fly into San José and drive [hours]. We have written the practical version of the whole valley: how to get here, what is worth a day, and which months are worth paying more for.

“The Vessyl is a sanctuary on the edge of the Arenal volcano, where nature, sound, and sensory experience are composed with intention.
Every space is built to help the nervous system settle and the mind grow still, so that presence returns on its own. It is less a place you visit than a set of conditions, carefully made, for feeling like yourself again.”
The Vessyl was designed and is run by Josh Stanley, who lives on the property.

You lie down on the floor of the Dome. The lights go low. For the next [x] minutes sound moves through the room and through the floor, so the low end arrives in your body before it arrives in your ears. Someone is running it live, watching the room, not pressing play on a file.

You keep your clothes on. There is water, and there are blankets, and you can leave at any point without explaining yourself. Nobody will talk to you about your chakras. 
We are not going to tell you what this will do for you. People come out of it quiet, and most of them sit outside for a while before they say anything. What that was worth is yours to decide.

if you are pregnant, have a pacemaker or another implanted device, or have a history of seizures, write to us first. There are a few things we will ask you to check with a doctor, and a few we will say no to, and we would rather say it now than at the door.
